standard.title: Specification for Cam Levers (कैम लीवर की विशिष्टि)
standard.sector: Production and General Engineering / Machine Tools, Machine Tool Elements, and Holding Devices

sectional_committee.name: Machine Tools, Machine Tool Elements, and Holding Devices Sectional Committee

standard.description: This Indian Standard specifies the physical dimensions, mechanical tolerances, materials, surface finish, and hardness thresholds for cam levers (eccentric clamping levers) used in combination with cam-operated clamps conforming to IS 6090 : 1984.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard specifies the physical dimensions, mechanical tolerances, materials, surface finish, and hardness thresholds for cam levers (eccentric clamping levers) used in combination with cam-operated clamps conforming to IS 6090 : 1984.

supersedes: None (Developed as a new dedicated specification for standard cam levers)

certification.description: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to obtain a valid BIS license to stamp or emboss the physical ISI 'Standard Mark' directly on the product packaging to certify metallurgical, structural, and dimensional conformity.
requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, dimensional parameters, and hardness readings must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The decimal places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
Specifies dimensions and other requirements for cam levers to be used with cam operated clamps conforming to IS : 6090 - 1984.
The lever body must be manufactured from high-grade case-hardened steel featuring a core tensile strength of 600 to 750 N/mm² to prevent shear fractures under rapid manual load cycles.

The eccentric cam contact face is subjected to intense sliding friction; therefore, the cam portion must be hardened to a minimum surface hardness of 680 HV (Vickers Hardness) to prevent flat-spots or surface pitting.

Standardizes physical proportions: Eccentricity e = 1.50 mm (clamping range finished to N6); Handle Length l = 63 mm; Pin Hole Diameter d = 6 mm (F7 fit); Width h = 16 mm; Cam Major Radius r = 16 mm; Radius r1 = 7.5 mm; Radius r2 = 8 mm; Head Height h1 = 31 mm (approx); and Thickness t = 6 mm.
The lever handle must be entirely free from sharp corners, burrs, forge scale, cracks, or parting-line offsets to protect the machine operator from hand cuts.

Levers must be designated by the name, eccentricity (e), handle length (l), standard number, and material. Example: 'CAM LEVER 3 x 125 IS : 10882 Steel' represents a lever of eccentricity e = 3 mm and handle length l = 125 mm.
